s0005: [1] Hello everyone! Today we will uncover the secrets of the most familiar numbers of all, the natural numbers: prime numbers, powers, and division with remainder. s0008: [1] A prime number is a number greater than one that is divisible only by one and itself: two, three, five, seven, eleven. [2] We divide thirty-six by the smallest primes one after another: by two, by two again, then by three. [3] We write repeated factors as powers: two squared times three squared.

s0011: [1] We write the prime factorizations of twelve and eighteen. [2] For the GCF, we take the factors found in both numbers, each to its lowest power. The result is six. [3] For the LCM, we take all the factors, each to its highest power. The result is thirty-six.
s0013: [1] When we multiply powers with the same base, we add the exponents. [2] For example, eight is two cubed, sixteen is two to the fourth power, and their product is two to the seventh power. [3] To rewrite a power of four as a power of two, we multiply the exponent by two.

s0044: We keep dividing by the smallest prime until the quotient is itself a prime. Twelve is two times six, and six is two times three. So twelve is made of two, two, and three.

s0148: [1] In winter the thermometer shows minus six degrees, and in summer plus thirty-five degrees. Today we will make friends with negative and positive numbers. [2] In the international TIMSS study, on average forty-two percent of students worldwide answered the question on this topic correctly. Today you will learn to solve it with confidence!
s0150: [1] On a number line, zero is in the middle, positive numbers are to the right, and negative numbers are to the left. [2] On a number line, the number further to the right is greater. Minus seven is to the left of minus three, so it is smaller.
s0153: [1] The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line. A distance is never negative. [2] Five and minus five are the same distance from zero but on different sides, so they are opposite numbers.
s0155: [1] If we move five steps to the right from minus eight, we reach minus three. [2] If we move nine steps to the left from four, we pass zero and land on minus five. [3] Subtracting a negative number means adding its opposite: three minus minus four is seven.
s0157: [1] If the signs are the same, the result is positive; if they are different, it is negative. The same goes for division. [2] Minus three times minus four is plus twelve; minus twenty divided by four is minus five.

s0160: [1] Example one: in the morning the temperature was minus six degrees, and during the day it rose by nine degrees. [2] We add nine to minus six: plus three degrees. [3] In the evening it dropped by eleven degrees: three minus eleven is minus eight degrees.

s0210: [1] A store has a twenty-five percent discount, and a recipe uses tea and sugar in a ratio of three to one. All of this is today's topic: ratio, proportion, and percent. [2] In the international TIMSS study, on average forty-three percent of students answered questions on this topic correctly. Today you will also learn to solve these questions with confidence!
s0212:
Ratio a : b — how many times as large a is as b
$12 : 18 = 2 : 3$
s0213: [1] A ratio compares two quantities: the ratio of a to b. [2] We simplify a ratio like a fraction: dividing twelve and eighteen by six gives a ratio of two to three.
s0215: [1] Two equal ratios form a proportion. In a proportion, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. [2] For example, if three fifths equals x over forty, then x is three times forty divided by five: twenty-four.
s0218: [1] One percent is one hundredth of a number. [2] To find p percent of a number, we multiply the number by p and divide by one hundred. [3] For example, fifteen percent of eighty is eighty times zero point one five, that is, twelve.
s0221: [1] A common problem: divide five hundred sixty in the ratio three to five. [2] Total parts: three plus five is eight. One part is five hundred sixty divided by eight: seventy. [3] The first gets three parts, two hundred ten, and the second gets five parts, three hundred fifty. Check: they add up to five hundred sixty.
s0224: [1] Example one: a jacket costs eighty thousand soums and has a twenty-five percent discount. [2] The discount amount is twenty-five percent of eighty thousand: twenty thousand soums. [3] The new price is eighty thousand minus twenty thousand: sixty thousand soums. Or, more quickly: seventy-five percent of eighty thousand.

s0280: [1] Five, eight, eleven, fourteen... Can you find the hundredth term without writing them all out? That is what we will learn today. [2] In the international TIMSS study, on average thirty-eight percent of students worldwide answered questions on this topic correctly. The formula for the nth term was especially hard, so today we will master exactly that!
s0283: [1] In a sequence, we look for how each number is made from the one before it. [2] Here three is added each time. So the next term is seventeen.
s0286: [1] If the same number d is added each time, the nth term equals the first term plus d added n minus one times. [2] In our sequence, the first term is five and the difference is three. Simplified: three n plus two. [3] Always check the formula: the fourth term should be fourteen, and it is.
s0288:
Figure n: $n \times n$ black square + red border
Total: $(n+2)^2$,  black: $n^2$
Red: $(n+2)^2 - n^2 = 4n + 4$
s0289: [1] Now shapes: figure n has n by n black tiles in the middle, surrounded by a border of one row of red tiles. [2] The whole figure is a square with side n plus two, so the total number of tiles is n plus two squared, and the black tiles number n squared. [3] To find the red tiles, we subtract the black tiles from the total: four n plus four.

s0292: [1] Sometimes a term is given and its position is asked for. To find it, we set the formula equal to that number. s0842: [1] If we toss a coin, will it land heads or tails? What is the chance of rolling a six on a die? Today we will learn to measure chance. [2] In the international TIMSS study, on average forty-nine percent of students worldwide answered questions on this topic correctly. Today you will learn to calculate probability exactly!
s0845: [1] Probability is the number of favorable outcomes divided by the number of all equally likely outcomes. [2] The probability of rolling a six on a die is one sixth, and the probability of rolling an even number is three sixths, that is, one half. [3] Probability goes from zero to one: an impossible event has probability zero, and a certain event has probability one.
s0848: [1] The probability that an event does not happen equals one minus its probability. [2] If the probability of rolling a six is one sixth, the probability of not rolling a six is five sixths.

s0851: [1] If an experiment is repeated N times, an event happens about P times N times. [2] For example, if one fourth of a spinner is red, in two hundred spins it will stop on red about fifty times. [3] This is an estimate: the actual result may differ a little from fifty.
